machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.3 (bundled, static); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-22, the day after the release (7.27.5 shipped without a report; a review found it). 7.27.4 and 7.27.5 each built from a git worktree of its tag, with the same .config and compiler; outputs_ext shared (linux-ext-libs 1.24 at both tags). In each tree only the kernel libraries, the modules, performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built (the whole SDK in the 7.27.5 tree, for the binary sizes). The `read` phase of `perf_timeranger2`, added for this report, was compiled into both trees: it uses only the public API, which did not change. The two binaries of each benchmark run alternately, the order flipped every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run (1 s for the three ctest binaries): 8 rounds, and 16 more for the four figures that came out of their noise after 8 (perf_tr_treedb, the TCP and TLS echo, the event loop echo with an append). The read path was measured apart: the `read` phase alone, 24 rounds, four binaries in rotation (7.27.4, 7.27.5, the main tree at 24da06bc8, and that tree with check_purge_before_read() made to return at once), a sync and a 1 s pause before each run. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The treedb figures are CPU time of the process per operation.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.27.5 are its side of the A/B run: the code of the tag, built on 2026-10-22 from a worktree of the tag on the machine of the earlier reports. Not a tag-time run: the release was tagged on 2026-10-21 without one. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass. The binary sizes are those of that build of the tag.

story.title: Yuneta 7.27.5: retention, and what it costs a replica to read
story.lead: 7.27.5 gives timeranger2 retention: a store deletes the old files of a key and keeps the `g_rowid` of every row that stays, and its followers hear the purge. It shipped without this report; a review found that, and that the read path of a replica had not been measured. Both are done here, the day after the release, on the machine of the earlier reports, 7.27.4 against 7.27.5, the two run alternately. A replica pays about 1 us more for every iterator open and every page, purged or not: one `stat()` that notices a purge whose signal it missed. That is +19% on a page of one row, +8% on an open, and noise on a page of 100 rows; the master does not pay it. The appends, the opens of a store, the treedb and the network move inside their noise, or by the placement of code that does not run.

hero.text: more per iterator open and per page on a replica: the price of noticing a purge it did not hear. A page of 100 rows does not see it (+0.8%), and the master does not pay it.

story.append_note: +0.4% against 7.27.4 (230,633): t = 0.6 over 8 alternated rounds; the append path refuses a record of a purged period at no measurable cost
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built twice, from the tree of each release, and the two binaries run alternately: 8 rounds, 24 for the read path and for the four figures that left their noise after 8. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, and what it buys. Three of them buy nothing: no code on their path changed, and they are said as measured.

ab.label: A page of 1 row, as a replica
ab.meaning: tranger2_iterator_get_page() of one row on a store another yuno writes: what a page costs beyond its rows.
ab.method: The read phase of perf_timeranger2 alone, 24 rounds, the binaries of 7.27.4, 7.27.5 and the main tree run in rotation, a sync and a 1 s pause before each run.
ab.reason: check_purge_before_read(): before every iterator open and every page, a replica stat()s the first md2 file of the key, to notice a purge of the master whose signal it did not hear (an overflow of its watch, a follower down while the master purged, a replica without a follower), before the read meets files that are gone. About 1 us per call on this machine, purged or not. With the check made to return at once, the same code reads at 7.27.4's speed (5.11 us): the check is all of it. Kept: skipping it while nothing seems missed leaves a window (a signal not yet read from the queue) in which a read opens a deleted file.

ab.reason: The same stat() of check_purge_before_read(), on a page of the index of a filtered iterator: +0.9 us. Without the check, 4.00 us (7.27.4: 3.98 us).
